title: Πιθήκου παῖδες
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 307 (= Perry 218). Text as printed. Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Τοὺς πιθήκους φασὶ δύο τίκτειν καὶ τὸ μὲν ἓν τῶν γεννημάτων στέργειν καὶ μετ’ ἐπιμελείας τρέφειν, τὸ δὲ ἕτερον μισεῖν καὶ ἀμελεῖν.
sentences.tr: Tous pithēkous phasi dyo tiktein kai to men hen tōn gennēmatōn stergein kai met’ epimeleias trephein, to de heteron misein kai amelein.
sentences.l: They say that monkeys bear two young, and that of their offspring the one they love and rear with care, but the other they hate and neglect.
sentences.n: φασί with accusative and infinitive is the standard way of reporting what is commonly said, and the whole sentence hangs on it — five infinitives under one verb. τὸ μὲν ἕν … τὸ δὲ ἕτερον is the μέν … δέ pair marking the two off against each other. στέργω is the affection that binds a family, the love of a parent for a child rather than desire.

sentences.t: Συμβαίνει δὲ κατά τινα θείαν τύχην τὸ μὲν ἐπιμελούμενον ἡδέως καὶ στερρῶς ἀγκαλιζόμενον παρὰ τῆς μητρὸς ἀποπνίγεσθαι, τὸ δὲ ὀλιγωρούμενον ἐκτελειοῦσθαι.
sentences.tr: Symbainei de kata tina theian tychēn to men epimeloumenon hēdeōs kai sterrōs ankalizomenon para tēs mētros apopnigesthai, to de oligōroumenon ekteleiousthai.
sentences.l: And it happens, by some divine chance, that the one cared for, being embraced fondly and hard by the mother, is choked to death, while the one made light of is brought to full growth.
sentences.i: And it comes about, by some divine chance, that the cherished one is embraced so fondly and so hard by its mother that it is smothered, while the neglected one grows up.
sentences.n: παρά with the genitive names the person a thing comes from, and so serves as the agent with a passive here. ἐπιμελέομαι is elsewhere a middle deponent, 'take care of'; τὸ ἐπιμελούμενον is its passive, 'the one being cared for', set against the passive τὸ ὀλιγωρούμενον. στερρῶς is 'stiffly, hard' — the tightness of the embrace, not its warmth, is what kills. ἐκτελειόω is to carry a thing through to its completion, and of a living creature that is to reach full growth.

sentences.t: Ὁ λόγος δηλοῖ ὅτι πάσης προνοίας ἡ τύχη δυνατωτέρα καθέστηκε.
sentences.tr: Ho logos dēloi hoti pasēs pronoias hē tychē dynatōtera kathestēke.
sentences.l: The story shows that chance has proved stronger than all forethought.
sentences.n: πάσης προνοίας is the genitive of comparison after δυνατωτέρα. καθέστηκε is the perfect of καθίστημι used intransitively: it has taken up that position and stands in it, so the perfect carries a present force.
